data.title: Fox News contributors denounce Trump's ban on CNN, MSNOW, Politico
data.description:
Several contributors to Fox News on Friday offered stark criticism of President Trump’s decision to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. 

Trump announced the decision in a Friday Truth Social post, saying the ban would be “effective immediately” for those outlets, “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” He suggested more outlets would be banned in the future.

Fox News Contributor Ari Fleischer was quick to respond on social media Friday, writing, “I agree with POTUS that several media outlets covering the WH are biased and unfair.”

“Banning them from the WH is not the solution. Open the pool and the briefing room to conservatives. Challenge liberal reporters. Argue and defeat them,” he stated. “Don’t ban them. Or one day they’ll ban us.”

Fox News’ Chief Political Analyst Brit Hume also wrote on social media that he “100%” agreed with a post from Jonathan Turley, a George Washington University Law School professor.

Turley called Trump’s move “terrible precedent and practice” that “would raise serious constitutional questions and undermine the country’s long-standing position as a voice for the free press.”

Hume added that if Trump “thinks this will lead to more favorable coverage, I think he’s dreaming.”

When asked in the Oval Office about the ban, Trump said he did it, “because they’re fake news. You get so tired of reading and seeing fake news.” 

“But our country has to have honest news,” he added.

The ban comes after Trump attempted to sue CNN for defamation for the outlet’s reporting on the 2020 election. He also sued the Wall Street Journal last year over its reporting on his alleged ties to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

data.title: Republican highlights man freed from ICE custody in campaign ad
data.description:
Rep. Monica De La Cruz (R-Texas) released a campaign advertisement featuring a man she helped get released Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody, along with his wife —who described the U.S.’s immigration system as “broken.”

The ad, which first aired last week, shows an interview with Weslaco, Texas woman whose husband — a Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipient — was detained by ICE.

The interviewee, named Stephanie, said he was freed after she reached out De La Cruz — the Texas 15th Congressional District incumbent locked in a tight race with Democratic challenger, Bobby Pulido.

“My husband and I did things the right way, but we were stuck in a broken immigration system,” Stephanie said. “We need to secure our borders to keep our families safe, but this immigration system is broken. So, we reached out to Monica de la Cruz.”

“She helped with my husband’s immigration case. I’ve voted Democrat before, but Monica puts people over politics,” the woman continued.

De La Cruz is not the first Latina Republican to break with President Trump on immigration. On Thursday, Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-Fla.) — running for reelection in Florida’s 27th Congressional District — released her own campaign video accusing the president of going “too far” with his escalated immigration enforcement operations.

“The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today,” Salazar said.

Both Salazar and De La Cruz represent predominately Hispanic districts, according to Census data.

Stephanie’s husband would not be the first person the Texas Republican has gotten out of ICE custody. In March, she escorted Antonio Gámez-Cuéllar, a teenager detained for nearly two weeks, out of an immigration detention facility to his loved ones.

“This is about our community coming together for, not only their family, but other families who are in similar situations,” De La Cruz said at the time, adding that her colleagues in Congress should work on “common sense” enforcement policies, the Texas Tribune reported.

De La Cruz faces a fierce challenge from Pulido, who gained traction within the 15th District.

An August poll from Texas Southern University’s Barbara Jordan Public Policy and Research and Survey Center reported that De La Cruz trailed Pulido by 5-points.

Cook Political Report July 16 update stated that “under normal circumstances, a district Trump carried by 18 points should not be competitive. But due to a number of unique factors” De La Cruz “faces a serious challenge from” Pulido. 

De La Cruz has ramped up campaign efforts as November approaches, both through releasing this ad and giving a speech at Trump’s Republican National Committee midterm convention.

But De La Cruz still praised Trump for his handling of the U.S. southern border, saying in her ad, “Working with President Trump, we ended the border crisis, and today that border is safer than any point in history.”

data.title: Trump touts Medicaid drug savings
data.description:
All 50 states, Washington, D.C. and Puerto Rico have applied to participate in an arrangement intended to give lower drug prices to Medicaid programs, President Trump said Friday. 

“This one thing alone should win us the midterms,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

Forty states and Puerto Rico have already signed agreements, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) said in a separate statement, and applying does not obligate states to participate. 

The administration’s “GENEROUS” model allows participating states to purchase drugs at a price aligned with those in other countries. The theory, according to the CMS, is that it will allow state Medicaid programs to benefit from fairer, more competitive pricing. 

The White House announcement comes as affordability concerns are at the forefront of voters’ concerns ahead of the November midterm elections. To try to address those concerns, Trump has cut deals with pharmaceutical companies so the cost of some drugs in the U.S. would be tied to what companies charge other wealthy countries.

But critics say the administration is merely papering over the issue, and has no real plan to deal with rising health costs— especially the ones caused when Republicans let ObamaCare’s enhanced premium subsidies expire.

The White House said participating pharmaceutical companies will provide state Medicaid programs with rebates on selected brand-name drugs to ensure the final price to Medicaid does not exceed what’s paid in other developed countries. 

More than two dozen drug companies have agreed to participate in the program, in exchange for tariff relief and exemptions from a similar pricing plan for Medicare. 

“Medicaid programs will get the best possible price for drugs, delivering better value for taxpayers and freeing up funds to give vulnerable Americans the high-quality care they deserve,” said CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz.  

The model includes hundreds of individual drugs, across virtually all major drug classes, including oncology, diabetes care, and asthma. 

The White House Council of Economic Advisers estimated the “most-favored nation” (MFN) deals in Medicaid will produce $36.6 billion in federal savings, and $27.6 billion for states.  

But Medicaid drugs are already subject to steep discounts, and many of the details of the agreements are secret, so the true impact of MFN agreements on drug costs and accessibility isn’t clear. 

 Critics said there’s little evidence that drug companies are meaningfully lowering prices at all.

“Big Pharma expects little to no financial impact from these short-term Medicaid deals. Instead, pharma companies and Trump appear to have worked together to offer minor concessions to avoid taking more meaningful action to lower prices,” Peter Maybarduk, Access to Medicines director for Public Citizen, said in a statement, calling the agreements a “charade.”

data.title: Here's how CNN, Politico and MS NOW are responding to Trump's White House ban
data.description:
President Trump’s threat to ban three national news outlets from covering the White House is sparking rebuke from First Amendment advocates, elected Democrats and critics from across politics and media.

In a Truth Social post on Friday afternoon, Trump wrote he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House “effective immediately” for what he said was “a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!”

The president also suggested more outlets could be banned in the future and said no specific story or segment was sparking the ban, adding, “it’s really just cumulative stories over the last two years. You get sick of it.”

As of Friday evening, no reporters from any of the outlets mentioned in the president’s Truth Social post had reported being kicked off the White House grounds and the White House Correspondents Association had not weighed in on the president’s post.

Here’s what each outlet has said about Trump’s social media threat.

CNN

The Warner Bros. Discovery-owned network pushed back on the president for suggesting he would bar its journalists from covering his White House and said removing them from the grounds could violate the law.

“CNN stands fully behind our White House team and their fair and accurate reporting,” a spokesperson for the outlet said. “We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do that reporting without hindrance or interference from the government.”

The cable news channel telegraphed potential legal action if Trump made good on his promise to keep its reporters from the White House.

“Should the ban which President Trump threatened go ahead, it would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right,” the spokesperson said.

Trump has a long history of attacking CNN over its coverage of him and has specifically targeted anchor and reporter Kaitlan Collins in recent weeks over her questioning of him in the Oval Office.

Politico

Politico, an outlet that became the target of right-wing scorn during Elon Musk’s efforts to trim government spending, was also included in what Trump said was a soon-to-be-banned list.

Musk took issue with Politico “Pro” subscriptions during DOGE efforts he led, a service that many government employees and departments subscribe to for information and reporting on the inner workings of the federal government.

Trump, in his Truth Social post, suggested Politico was reporting “fake news” about him while benefiting from what he characterized as government subsidies.

“POLITICO will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones,” the outlet said in a statement to The Hill on Friday. “We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them,” a spokesperson for the outlet said.

Of the accusations the outlet was taking money from the federal government, the outlet said, “the claims that POLITICO received government subsidies are false and have been thoroughly debunked.”

MS NOW

MS NOW declined to comment on the president’s threat, but its hosts and personalities have frequently been critical of Trump and his policies for years.

The progressive cable channel, formerly known as MSNBC, is home to the morning political talk program “Morning Joe,” which the president has attacked on numerous occasions during his years in office, and former Biden press secretary Jen Psaki.

data.title: Kirk Herbstreit defends having Ted Cruz on 'College GameDay'
data.description:
Football analyst and ESPN personality Kirk Herbstreit defended the network’s decision to have Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) on the network’s flagship college football pregame show last week.

“We had him on because they were going to be voting this week,” Herbstreit told reporters on Friday, referring to the “Protect College Sports Act” (PCSA), a Senate bill looking to regulate the big business of college sports around issues such as the transfer portal, revenue sharing and name image and likeness money paid to student athletes.

“Maybe he could give us some insight into what’s going on,” Herbstreit said of Cruz, who has championed the bipartisan legislation with Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.). “That was really it. We’re not picking any sides in any way at all. We just want to see the chaos that’s kind of surrounding this sport kind of be reeled in and if this helps us get to that then great.”

ESPN has faced criticism from the the bill’s detractors over Cruz’s appearance on the highly rated sports talk show.

Several days later, the network had NAACP President Derrick Johnson on an evening episode of “SportsCenter” to speak about his group’s opposition to the bill.

During his nearly 10 minute long visit with anchor Rece Davis, Cruz argued the PCSA must be passed to “fix” the issues facing college sports saying “the current situation is nuts …. the reason Congress is acting is because Congress created this problem.”

The Republican was met with boos by the live audience in Austin, Texas, during his appearance.

“The guy that sits right next to me, Nick Saban, was part of putting this together. This guy loves college football more than anybody I’ve met,” Herbstreit said. “And so if he’s happy about what this would do, then I’ll follow his lead.”

Despite opposition from a number of Democrats and GOP holdouts, the bill cleared its first major congressional tests last week, winning the backing of more than 70 senators on two procedural votes. It is expected to face a final vote next week.

With the House out of session until after the midterm elections, the soonest the PCSA could get to President Trump for his signature is November.

data.title: Trump: US strikes security deal with Greenland, Denmark
data.description:
President Trump said Friday that the United States has entered a security agreement with Greenland and Denmark that gives America a bigger say in the Arctic territory’s affairs and expands its military presence in the country. 

Trump said the deal “gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many U.S. concerns.”

“Additionally, from now on, no U.S. adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval,” he added in a post online.

The Hill is seeking comment from officials representing Greenland and Denmark, which owns the independently governed island. 

Trump infuriated Greenland and its allies in NATO with demands for U.S. ownership of the island earlier this year. The deal outlined by Trump appears to fall short of that desire.

The president has argued that greater U.S. control of the island is necessary to ensure it doesn’t fall into the hands of China or Russia amid growing competition over the Arctic. 

“We will immediately begin the process of developing a large Military presence in the appropriate part of Greenland, of which there are many,” Trump wrote in his post. “We will work with the people of Greenland in its development and construction.”

DEVELOPING…

data.title: El-Sayed challenges Vance to weightlifting competition: 'You talk a good game'
data.description:
Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed (D) responded Friday to Vice President Vance’s disses on his appearance, saying he’d challenge President Trump’s second-in-command to a weightlifting competition to prove whether he’s “as strong as he likes to pretend he is.”

TMZ DC asked El-Sayed about a TikTok post earlier this week where Vance joked about the Democratic nominee having a “patchy beard,” to which he responded with his own jabs at the vice president’s looks.

The Michigan Democrat said, “If I actually met [Vance], I’d be like, ‘All right, let’s just actually see. How much paste did you have to put on your face to get that little beard?’”

“J.D., listen, man. You talk a good game. You went to Ohio State. Didn’t even know how to handle the trophy when you pick it up, right? And now you’re on, what? Like juiced up on TRT [Testosterone Replacement Therapy]. I’m all natural, bro,” El-Sayed continued, before adding he’d be “happy to invite him to any weight room, in any place.”

“And at the end of the day, the bigger question, my issue with you, is not your beard, right? As much as you want to make it about my beard. My issue with you is that you, you are out here riding policy that you know is stupid … and then you try to act the tough guy, because you can’t be the tough guy to the actual boss, because you’re afraid of him.”

El-Sayed and the vice president have gone tit-for-tat with insults throughout the midterm election cycle. During an August campaign-style rally, Vance called the Senate candidate “very, very evil.”

Trump has similarly targeted El-Sayed, previously labeling him as “crazy,” a “jihadist” and a “Communist loser who hates Jews and Israel.”

“Well, let me tell you what’s evil,” El-Sayed said when asked about Vance’s August remarks. “Evil is the idea of starting wars when there’s peace. Evil is the idea of stripping away people’s healthcare when they absolutely have no other option. What’s evil is to do that, so that you can pass a tax cut for billionaires.”

The vice president has also been critical of El-Sayed’s association with political commentator and Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, whose 2019 comments saying the U.S. deserved the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks drew criticism ahead of November’s midterms.

El-Sayed disavowed Piker’s controversial statement, for which the streamer has since apologized.

El-Sayed is facing off against former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) in a key battleground state that former President Biden won in 2020 and Trump won in 2024.

data.title: Trump says he still backs Salazar after video criticizing him on immigration
data.description:
President Trump said he still supports Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-Fla.) but disagrees with her on immigration one day after her campaign rolled out an ad criticizing the president on the policy issue. 

“She obviously doesn’t have a very strong feeling about the border. I do,” Trump told reporters when asked about the vieo in the Oval Office on Friday. 

“I’m very strong on the borders and she isn’t. And she’s a nice person. I got her elected. Without me, she wouldn’t have gotten elected,” he continued. 

Salazar’s campaign released an ad on Thursday accusing the administration of going “too far” on federal immigration enforcement operations. 

“The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today,” Salazar, who’s running for reelection in November, said in the clip.

“You can be for immigration what Lincoln was for slavery and Reagan was for communism,” the Republican continued. “I’m not talking about giving them amnesty. I’m talking about giving them a dignified life in this promised land.” 

The ad will run on television and online in South Florida. 

Trump endorsed Salazar in a Truth Social post last February, praising her “Wisdom and Courage” in confronting “the Corrupt Fake News.”

Salazar is running against Democratic candidate Eliott Rodriguez in the state’s 27th Congressional District, which she has represented since 2021. The district, which includes parts of Miami, houses one of the highest foreign-born populations of any House district in the country.

data.title: Trump says son paid back Russian oligarch for wedding gift
data.description:
President Trump said Friday that his son, Donald Trump Jr., paid back the Russian oligarch that funded some of his lavish wedding celebrations after concerns flared over ethics violations and potential influences from foreign adversaries.

Trump was asked in the Oval Office whether it was appropriate that his son accepted the gift from Umar Kremlev after his wedding to socialite Bettina Anderson.

“Well, it’s totally allowed, and a lot of people have parties, and all, but it’s totally allowed,” Trump said. “But as I understand it, he paid him back. He didn’t want to have that, so I hear he paid him back.”

The amount was reportedly hundreds of thousands of dollars and went toward after-party affairs, including a private island in the Bahamas and a fireworks show, according to a ProPublica investigation published earlier this week.

A spokesperson for Trump Jr. didn’t deny the payments and said the oligarch, Umar Kremlev, was a friend of his.

In an Instagram post the couple also defended the gift, calling it “an extraordinarily generous wedding gift from a friend.”

“A person that he knows, I guess a friend of his, gave him a wedding party – that’s very common,” Trump said Friday. “I’ve heard of many people giving wedding parties.”

“I’ve given wedding parties for numerous people,” he added.

Kremlev is the head of the International Boxing Association (IBA), a controversy-plagued sports organization financed by Russia’s state-owned natural gas company, Gazprom. 

He is also a close ally to Russian President Vladimir Putin and reportedly traveled with him to China ahead of Trump Jr.’s wedding.

Democrats were quick to condemn the wedding gift, calling it corruption.

data.title: Court reinstates $7B 'Solar for All' program axed by Trump
data.description:
A federal court has rebuffed the Trump administration’s effort to slash a $7 billion program that seeks to provide rooftop solar power in disadvantaged communities. 

Judge Mary McElroy, a Trump appointee in Rhode Island, vacated the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) move to terminate the Solar For All (SFA) program and claw back the funding.

The program in question was funded by the Biden administration’s Inflation Reduction Act. The Trump-era One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) rescinded any “unobligated” balances in the program.

McElroy said that under these laws, the EPA did not have the power to rescind funds that were already awarded.

“The OBBBA did not convert SFA funding into a lump-sum amount subject to EPA’s discretion. Instead, Congress’s clear intent was that EPA continue to administer the already obligated SFA grants. Defendants acted contrary to this intent, and with no other statutory authority, when they terminated the SFA program,” she wrote. 

The judge therefore declared the program’s termination unlawful and tossed out the EPA’s move to do so.

Her decision represents a blow to the Trump administration’s efforts to reduce government spending and target Biden-era climate programs.

An EPA spokesperson said in an email that it is “reviewing the decision and considering options for appeal.”

Environmental advocates, including those who sued over the decision, lauded the judge’s ruling.

“The court ruled the Trump Administration never should have terminated Solar for All because Congress intended it to continue, and EPA broke the law when it killed the program and pocketed the money,” said Southern Environmental Law Center senior attorney Nick Torrey in a written statement  “Electricity bills are skyrocketing, so low-cost solar projects — which guarantee big savings — are needed now more than ever. Today’s victory means EPA must stop sitting on the $7 billion in funding for this program and start getting it out into communities to provide hardworking American families much-needed relief.”
